channel.title: Parallax
channel.description: Same event, different vantage points. Geopolitical news compared across Western, Eastern, Middle Eastern and Russian outlets.

item.title: Russian drone strikes in the Kyiv region result in multiple casualties and reported injuries.
item.description: On November 23, 2026, a Russian drone strike destroyed a five-story residential building in the Dymer area of the Kyiv region, causing multiple casualties. Western outlets focus on the humanitarian crisis, emphasizing the immediate human toll and the rescue efforts for victims in Ukraine. In contrast, Russian-aligned sources frame the event as part of a reciprocal cycle of escalation, frequently pairing the report of the strike with Ukrainian drone strikes on the Belgorod Region.

item.title: Israeli settlers and forces conduct a series of attacks and cause fires in West Bank villages.
item.description: On November 23, 2026, vehicles and property were set ablaze in several West Bank villages, prompting an official Israeli investigation and a military response. Western outlets frame the incident as a domestic legal issue, focusing on internal Israeli political backlash and the condemnation of "settler violence." Conversely, Middle Eastern sources frame the events as a systemic pattern of aggression, emphasizing the psychological impact on Palestinian residents and the broader scope of escalating hostilities.

item.title: Russian warship hit by suspected drone attack at a naval base in Libya
item.description: On November 23, 2026, a Russian warship at the Benghazi naval base in Libya was struck by an explosion, which local authorities identified as a suspected drone attack. While all sources confirm the strike occurred with no reported casualties, coverage differs significantly in its framing of the incident's scope. Western outlets focus on the potential link to the Ukraine conflict, whereas Middle Eastern reporting emphasizes regional maritime security and the involvement of a second nearby vessel.

item.title: Israeli official condemns settler attacks in the West Bank as acts of Jewish terrorism.
item.description: Israeli politician Gadi Eisenkot condemned a series of arson attacks and racist graffiti in Palestinian villages near Ramallah as "Jewish terrorism." While all sources report the condemnation and the resulting internal friction regarding right-wing ministers, coverage diverges on the primary framing of the incident. Middle Eastern outlets emphasize the violence as a result of government-fueled policies and international pressure, whereas other reports focus more on the internal political fallout and domestic implications.
